body_html:
What makes a good blank t-shirt for printing?

A blank is only as good as the print that ends up on it. Printers look at four things before anything else:

  • Fabric and weight. 100 % cotton between approx. 145 and 195 g/m² takes screen print, DTG and vinyl well. Lighter shirts are cheaper and cooler; heavier ones feel more solid and are less sheer in white.
  • A smooth, tubular body. The classic Fruit of the Loom tees are knitted as a tube with no side seams, so the print area is flat and the shirt lies evenly on a screen pallet or heat press.
  • Colour and size range. A group order needs the same shirt in every size from XS to XXXL, and a merch run needs more than black and white.
  • Consistency. Fruit of the Loom's product codes (61-036, 61-082 and so on) have been stable for years, so a reorder matches the first batch in cut, weight and colour.

That combination is why Fruit of the Loom is one of the standard blanks in European print workshops, next to Gildan and B&C. Our {{LINK:printing|guide to printing on Fruit of the Loom}} covers the techniques in depth; this article is about choosing and buying the blank itself.

White, black or colour: what changes for the print?

The garment colour affects both the price of the print and the result:

  • White and light colours are the easiest to print. DTG needs no white underbase, so full-colour and photo prints are cheaper and sharper.
  • Black and dark colours need a white underbase for DTG and often an extra screen in screen printing. Expect a slightly higher print price per piece.
  • Heather (marl) colours contain polyester. They print well with screen print and vinyl, but tell your printer, because high heat can behave differently on the blend.
  • Sublimation only works on polyester, so it is not an option on 100 % cotton blanks. Use DTG or DTF for full-colour designs instead.

For a white shirt that should not look sheer, choose the Valueweight (approx. 165 g/m²) or the Heavy Cotton (approx. 195 g/m²) rather than the lighter Original T.

Checklist before you order blanks for printing

  1. Agree the model with your printer. Give them the product code (e.g. 61-036) so they set up for the right fabric and print area.
  2. Split the sizes realistically. For mixed adult groups, M and L usually make up the largest share. Our {{LINK:size-guide|Fruit of the Loom size guide}} lists chest widths per size.
  3. Add a few spares. Ordering approx. 5 % extra covers misprints and late sign-ups.
  4. Order one sample first if you are trying a new colour, so you can check shade and fabric before the full run.
  5. Ship blanks straight to the printer if you can — enter the print shop as the delivery address and save a trip.
  6. Plan the timing. Blanks from Marmalade Co. arrive in 2–3 business days; most print shops then need around 1–2 weeks.

faq.q: What is the best blank t-shirt for printing?
faq.a: For most jobs the Fruit of the Loom Valueweight T (61-036) is the safest choice: approx. 165 g/m² of 100 % cotton, a tubular body without side seams, a wide colour range and sizes from XS to XXXL. It takes screen print, DTG and vinyl well. Choose the heavier Heavy Cotton T for workwear or the lighter Original T for large giveaway runs.

(marmaladeco.com) sells blank Fruit of the Loom t-shirts to anyone from one piece, at €6.95 each with VAT included, 10 % off from 5 pieces and a flat €7 DHL shipping fee to 11 EU countries. faq.q: How much do blank t-shirts cost in bulk?
faq.a: At Marmalade Co. a blank Fruit of the Loom t-shirt costs €6.95, or approx. €6.26 from 5 pieces. With one €7 shipping fee per order, 100 blank tees come to approx. €632.50 delivered, about €6.33 per shirt, VAT included. Sizes and colours of the same shirt count together for the discount.

faq.q: Can I sublimate on Fruit of the Loom t-shirts?
faq.a: Not on the classic cotton tees. Sublimation ink only bonds with polyester, so it does not work on 100 % cotton blanks such as the Valueweight, Original or Heavy Cotton T. For full-colour designs on cotton, use DTG or DTF transfers instead; for simple logos in large runs, screen printing is the cheapest option.

faq.q: Are white Fruit of the Loom t-shirts see-through?
faq.a: The lighter models can show a little in white, especially the Original T at approx. 145 g/m². For a more opaque white blank, choose the Valueweight T (approx. 165 g/m²) or the Heavy Cotton T (approx. 195 g/m²). White is also the cheapest colour to print with DTG because no white underbase is needed.
